meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Habitually or in general. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take', paired with 'взять'.
'брать' alone often means this, in talk about officials

examples.trans: We have to take all the money.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: in questions: а вдруг...? = and what if...?
А вдруг... = what if. Core Russian adv meaning 'suddenly; all of a sudden' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level?

examples.text: Почему он вдруг сравнялся? Мы шли впереди на десять процентов!
examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level? We were ten percent ahead!

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must, should; owe').

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('living, alive, live').

examples.trans: Cutting a living person with a knife!
You can't torture a living person like that!

examples.text: Нина, ну как ты могла? Живого человека ножом резать!
examples.trans: Nina, how could you? Cutting a living person with a knife!

meanings.note: Verbal action or result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание', meaning 'will' in conversational and formal Russian.

examples.text: Папа испугался и пишет своё завещание!
examples.trans: Papa got scared and is writing his will!

examples.text: Папа испугался и сразу начал писать завещание!
examples.trans: Dad got scared and immediately started writing his will!

examples.text: Нотариус прочитал семье последнее завещание дедушки.
examples.trans: The notary read the grandfather's last will to the family.

meanings.note: Asks about the purpose. Core Russian adv meaning 'what for, why' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: In one direction, now. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.
To run for a second term. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'crucian carp' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это почти то же самое, что карась.
examples.trans: It is almost the exact same thing as a carp.

examples.text: Ты знал, что у него синий пояс по карате?
examples.trans: Did you know that he has a blue belt in karate?

examples.text: Скрипач и каратист, я бы сходил на такое кино!
examples.trans: A violinist and karate fighter, I would go see that movie!

meanings.note: Чн is pronounced шн. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Comparative of хорошо. Core Russian adv meaning 'better' in everyday speech.
лучший в мире = the best in the world
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('best; better').

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'milligram' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Одного миллиграмма её яда хватит, чтобы убить.
examples.trans: One milligram of its poison is enough to kill.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть миллиграмм.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always milligram.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
used with не before the verb, or alone

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам очень дорого обходится авторская кухня.
examples.trans: Auteur cuisine costs us very dearly.

examples.text: Это все, кто выходил из отеля.
examples.trans: That is everyone who left the hotel.
What is going on here right now?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: ничего не осталось = there's nothing left

Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remain, to be left', paired with 'оставаться'.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Used as an exclamation of approval. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лично'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Отлично, Ваня! Вот это твой образ!
examples.trans: Perfect, Vanya! That right there is your look!

meanings.note: Сделать ошибку = to make a mistake. Common feminine noun meaning 'mistake, error' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are many serious mistakes in the case.

examples.text: А прокуратура думает иначе. В деле много грубых ошибок.
examples.trans: The prosecutor's office thinks otherwise. There are many serious mistakes in the case.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'bet', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Впрочем, как и всегда, я выиграл пари!
examples.trans: As always, I won the bet!

examples.text: Я выиграл пари и доказал свою правоту.
examples.trans: I won the bet and proved I was right.

meanings.note: In a lesson. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to write', paired with 'написать'.
In a lesson. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to write', paired with 'написать'.
Irregular plural повара. Common masculine noun meaning 'cook, chef' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: In потому что. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'тому').
Потому и = that's exactly why. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'тому').

examples.text: Я устал, потому что много работал.
examples.trans: I'm tired because I worked a lot.
I'm at home because I'm ill.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'almost, nearly' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Наш с вами город очень старый. Почти четыре века здесь были набеги.
examples.trans: Our town is very old. For almost four centuries there were raids here.

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to cook, to make (food), to prepare
meanings.note: Takes accusative. Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to prepare, to cook, to make', paired with 'готовить'.

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'знавать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to admit, to recognise', paired with 'признать'.

Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'знавать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to admit, to recognise', paired with 'признать'.

examples.text: То есть вы признаёте свою ошибку?
То есть вы признаёте, что брали взятки?
examples.trans: So you admit that you took bribes?

examples.text: Там сидит критик, умей спокойно признавать ошибки.
examples.trans: A critic is sitting there, learn to calmly admit mistakes.

meanings.note: Imperative 'прощайте' = farewell. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'щать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to forgive; bid farewell'.

Imperative 'прощайте' = farewell. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'щать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to forgive; bid farewell'.

examples.text: Тогда прощай, я должен срочно уйти.
examples.trans: Then farewell, I must urgently leave.

meanings.note: Animal or food. Common feminine noun meaning 'fish' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A big platter of fish and crabs.

examples.text: На ужин мы приготовили свежую рыбу.
examples.trans: For dinner we cooked fresh fish.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the most; the very').

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: almost always the short form: я согласен (man), я согласна (woman)

A whole portion; completed action. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ъесть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to eat (up)', paired with 'есть'.

examples.text: Скоро. А пока я есть хочу, слона бы съел!
examples.trans: Soon. But for now I'm hungry, I could eat an elephant!

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Our restaurant is located right here.

examples.text: Мы теперь работаем в этом отеле.
examples.trans: We now work in this hotel.
How does a hotel restaurant differ?

meanings.note: At that time. Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.
Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'too, also' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

examples.trans: Do you want to kill me?

examples.text: Ты смотришь на меня так, как будто убить хочешь.
examples.trans: You look at me as if you want to kill me.

уметь.gloss: to know how to, to be able to

meanings.note: + infinitive: a learned skill. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'меть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know how to, to be able to', paired with 'суметь'.

examples.text: Эх, Паша, Паша. Ты считать не умеешь.
examples.trans: Oh, Pasha, Pasha. You can't count.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'fugu, pufferfish' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: They brought him that fugu fish.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть фугу.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always fugu.

meanings.note: impersonal, + genitive: денег не хватило = there wasn't enough money
Хватит!. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be enough', paired with 'хватать'.

examples.trans: Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

+ infinitive. Core Russian conj meaning 'so that, in order to' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm calling to say thank you.
So that there are witnesses, Samson.

points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.
